parsed.summary: The file states four results. (1) A spherical-code bound: for interlacing (a,b) with 2Γ_r(a,b) > s and any R > Φ_r(a,b), every s-code in ℝ^n eventually has fewer than 2^{Rn} points, so R_sph(s) is at most the closed-constraint hierarchy infimum. (2) The strict hierarchy of level and cap-localized exponents, ending in equality of the level-0 localized rate with the localized Kabatianskii–Levenshtein bound. (3) A binary-code bound that is strictly below MRRW. (4) An eventual kissing-number bound 2^{0.39661n}. The main caveats: the binary-code definitions and the 0.39661 constant are not in the excerpt and cannot be checked; and the Lean κ_r uses the strict constraint 2Γ > s where the paper uses 2Γ ≥ s.

glossary.plain: Finite sets of unit vectors in ℝ^n with pairwise inner products ≤ s; A(n,s) is the sup of their cardinalities in ℕ∞.
Γ_r = Σ_ℓ R_ℓ·√(x_ℓ)/(1+2a_ℓ), with x = a(1+a) and Lagrange weights R_ℓ = ∏_m(x_ℓ−y_m)/∏_{j≠ℓ}(x_ℓ−x_j).
glossary.note: The excerpt's formula is garbled. A consistency check works: r=1 with a_2=0 reduces exactly to the one-row MetricCodes.Gamma.

glossary.plain: Φ_r = Σ h(a_ℓ) − Σ h(b_m), where h(u) = (1+u)log₂(1+u) − u log₂ u
glossary.note: Not fully legible in the excerpt.
A(n,s) is finite for s<1, so toNat is harmless.

glossary.plain: κ_r(s) = inf Φ_r over level-r interlacing tuples with 2Γ_r > s
glossary.standard_concept: κ_r(s), the inner infimum with 2Γ_r ≥ s
glossary.note: Uses a strict constraint; the paper uses a closed one.
κ_r(0)=0 holds automatically via the infimum (a→0).
The KL formula matches with u = (1−sinθ)/(2sinθ).

glossary.plain: One-row exponent inf h(a)−h(b) over 0<b<a with s < 2Γ(a,b), then localized
glossary.note: Equals level 1 with a_2=0, as the paper describes.

glossary.plain: min over 0≤u≤1−2δ of 1 + g(u²) − g(u²+2δu+2δ), with g(x) = H((1−√(1−x))/2)
glossary.note: The argument stays ≤ 1, so no sqrt junk occurs.

lean_claims.plain: For 0<s<1, the following holds. (i) For every r, interlacing (a,b) with s < 2Γ_r(a,b), and R > Φ_r(a,b): for all sufficiently large n, every s-code C in ℝ^n has |C| < 2^{Rn}. (ii) limsup log₂A(n,s)/n ≤ inf{Φ_r(a,b) : r, interlacing, s ≤ 2Γ_r}.

For 0<s<1, the following all hold. For every r: κ_{r+1}(s) < κ_r(s) and κ̄_{r+1}(s) < κ̄_r(s), where κ̄ is the localized rate. Further, R_sph(s) ≤ inf_r κ̄_r(s) < κ̄_1(s) < κ̄_row(s) < κ̄_0(s) = localized KL(s).
For all sufficiently large n, the kissing number in dimension n is ≤ 2^{0.39661 n}.
For 0<δ<1/2, the following holds. limsup log₂A(n,⌈δn⌉)/n ≤ min(Hamming variational rate, Johnson variational rate), and this minimum is strictly less than the MRRW bound.

paper_claims.plain: If 2Γ_r(a,b) > s then A(n,s) ≤ 2^{(Φ_r+o(1))n}; hence R_sph(s) ≤ inf over r and tuples with 2Γ_r ≥ s of Φ_r.

For every 0<s<1 and r≥0: κ_{r+1} < κ_r for both the plain and the cap-localized exponents. Also R_sph ≤ inf κ̄_r < κ̄_1 < κ̄_row < κ̄_0 = B_KL. Corollary 7.6 adds the plain inequalities κ_1 < κ_row < κ_0.

coverage.why: 'Eventually < 2^{Rn} for each R > Φ' is equivalent to the o(1) form; the corollary uses the closed constraint, as in the paper.
The plain-exponent chain κ_1 < κ_row < κ_0 from Corollary 7.6 is omitted. Separately, κ_r is defined with the strict constraint.
The constant is not in the excerpt, so it cannot be compared.
Covered elsewhere (sibling file); definitions cannot be verified from this excerpt.

flags.explanation: The paper's κ_r is the inner infimum with 2Γ_r ≥ s; Lean uses s < 2Γ_r. The two agree only if closed-boundary points at a fixed level r can be approximated by strictly feasible ones at the same level. The paper states this approximation without specifying the level; it is not shown at fixed r in the excerpt.

flags.explanation: The non-localized inequalities κ_1 < κ_row < κ_0 are not stated.

flags.explanation: The constant 0.39661 does not appear in the excerpt, so the statement cannot be checked against the paper. The bound is ≤ eventually, not including an o(1).

The Hamming and Johnson variational rates (spectralLimit, rankPenalty, AsymptoticParameters) are bespoke and absent from this excerpt; their fidelity must be checked against the sibling paper section. The MRRW definition matches the standard one.

All rates use sInf in ℝ. If a set were empty or unbounded below, the rate would be 0, which would change meaning. The sets appear nonempty (e.g. level 0 with large a gives 2Γ→1) and bounded below, but this is not stated.
